verdicts.note: Racial-ethnic disparities in privately-insured antidepressant use.
Male rats. Wall 7.
Dementia.

SIGN-REVERSING RECORD. Psychiatric intervention IMPROVED pregnancy rates in infertile couples. Call 2's ambiguity observed: treating the indication raises fertility. Clinic-selected population, and the intervention is not cleanly pharmacological, so it is a parameter rather than a primary estimate.
Postpartum women treated for depression. Post-birth, so it speaks to subsequent parity rather than first conception.
Male rats. Wall 7.
Rat seminiferous epithelium. Wall 7.
Monoamine theory and the development of the drug class. Book chapter.

KEY PARAMETER RECORD. PATERNAL prescription medication in the months BEFORE conception, all births in a national cohort. Preconception exposure prevalence is the quantity the significance computation needs and the one pregnancy-conditioned series systematically understate.

KEY BASELINE RECORD. Own and PARTNER'S depression against CHILDLESSNESS, nationwide register, in Social Science and Medicine. The indication's effect stated as a completed-fertility outcome, and the partner dimension is one no medication study in this frame has.
Sexual side effects with and without naltrexone.
Muscle and cardiometabolic health.
Male rats, sexual behaviour. Wall 7 — and note it is the only place the behavioural pathway is tested experimentally at all.
Depression AND its treatment against semen parameters. Both exposures, mechanism outcome.

Pratt et al., NCHS Data Brief: 11% of Americans aged 12+ on antidepressants, 2005-2008. Recovers as a frame record the anchor A3 could not key to a DOI, which is the expected fate of an agency series.
Antidepressant use around the time of pregnancy, US population.
MDD and antidepressant treatment together as causes of dysfunction.
Double-blind randomised PLACEBO-CONTROLLED fixed-dose ejaculation study. The strongest identification available anywhere in this chapter, on link 1.
Treatment-response prediction.
Double-blind comparison of sexual functioning in depressed outpatients.
Adverse outcome pathway analysis for FISH. Wall 7.
Heart defects. Wall 4.
Occupational exposures and semen quality. B.2's exposure.
Fertility and Sterility, psychiatric considerations in male fertility. No abstract on the record.

Vaginal lubricants and natural fertility. Wrong determinant, but a useful design analogue: a small mechanical impediment measured against a fecundability outcome is the shape B.7's evidence would need.
Villous trophoblast cells; placental mechanism for Wall 4 outcomes.
Bias in estimating fecundability parameters across statistical models. Bears on whether TTP estimates from different cohorts can be compared at all.
Medical therapies causing IATROGENIC male infertility, Fertility and Sterility. Frames B.7's claim as one entry in a drug list; no abstract on the record.
New-onset diabetes.

SIGN-REVERSING RECORD. Sexual function IMPROVES as depressive symptoms fall under escitalopram. The therapeutic benefit at link 1, and the direct counter-case to reading link 1 as a uniform decrement. Call 2 rests on records like this one.
JEG-3 and HIPEC placental cell models.
Females in REMISSION on escitalopram, which partly holds symptom severity fixed.

KEY PARAMETER RECORD. Prevalence and sociodemographic patterns of antidepressant use among WOMEN OF REPRODUCTIVE AGE, in Journal of Affective Disorders. The exact denominator population the significance computation needs. No abstract on the record.
Switching to reverse fluoxetine-induced dysfunction.
Adjunct safety and tolerability.
Statistical models for human fecundability.
BMI and health risk; journal version of the York thesis record.
Infertility associated with depression, anxiety and distress. The reverse arrow as a review.
Suicide attempt.
Acupressure for sexual function under antidepressants.
Patient perspectives on LONG-TERM antidepressant use. Duration of use is the deflator in the quantum calculation and is poorly measured by dispensing records.

THE ONLY LINK-2 RECORD IN THE FRAME SO FAR, and it is a phenomenological interview study of how women taking SSRIs cope with sexual difficulties — behaviour, not function. A qualitative dissertation in a university repository. The chain's second joint is evidenced by this and nothing else, which is the scope document's prediction confirmed in the sharpest possible way.
StatsRef entry on fertility studies and exposure effects.
Omani tertiary-hospital utilisation.
IUI Cochrane review.
Length of prenatal exposure. Wall 4.
Benzodiazepine-SSRI combination for comorbid anxiety.

KEY LINK-3 RECORD. Mistiming of intercourse as a PRIMARY cause of failure to conceive. It says directly that when conception fails for behavioural reasons the binding factor is timing rather than frequency — which is the finding that shrinks any libido-based fertility effect.
In vitro cell mechanism.
Upper GI bleeding.
Pharmacovigilance disproportionality; spontaneous-report ascertainment.
Paediatric safety.
Cardiac events in Parkinson's.
Gastrointestinal symptoms.

Prescribing to youth with MINIMAL OR MILD depression. Bears on Call 2: where the indication is mild, the therapeutic benefit that offsets the pharmacological decrement is smallest, so the net effect is most likely negative in exactly this group.
Characteristics of depressed patients NOT receiving antidepressants. The untreated-indicated comparison group Wall 1 asks for, described.
Efficacy and safety for MDD.

KEY METHODOLOGICAL ANALOGUE. Demography: temperature shocks and DYNAMIC ADJUSTMENT in US birth rates. A transient shock to conception followed by rebound, estimated as displacement rather than as lost births — the exact tempo-versus-quantum decomposition B.7's exposure-duration deflator needs, executed on a different shock. Not evidence about antidepressants; a template for how to convert one into a birth count.
Environmental toxins and male fertility. B.2/B.6.
Persistent dysfunction after discontinuation. Persistence matters for the deflator: if the decrement outlives the exposure, the short-episode argument weakens.
